page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware configuration provisions 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, capable of clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports modern vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. System memory is sized at 256.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong per-thread computational capability. Single-core evaluations place the instance in the top tier, scoring 2877.0 in Geekbench and 3783.48 in stress-ng single-core tests. Compression throughput is notably high, achieving 41.24 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 18.16 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. The PassMark CPU score of 56708.47 and PassMark memory score of 2815.72 fall into the top 25 percent bracket. Potentially uncached memory bandwidth registers at 103.4 GB/sec for large-block reads and 68.56 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high memory density per core, making it effective for systems where memory capacity drives deployment size rather than raw execution core counts. A key operational tradeoff is the complete reliance on network storage for root and ephemeral filesystems. Furthermore, while the instance handles prompt processing and small language model inference well, executing large 70B parameter models on CPU results in poor throughput at 2.37 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

Given its memory density, strong single-thread performance, and dedicated vCPU topology, Microsoft Azure E32as_v7 is well structured for in-memory caching clusters such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, large software compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive extract-transform-load (ETL) processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 32 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, backed by a 16-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of 4.5 GHz clock speeds. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features dedicated core allocation, 32 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 vector support. With no integrated local storage or GPU acceleration, storage relies on external network volumes like Premium Storage. Benchmarks show high single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and gzip compression scoring in the top decile, alongside upper-quartile PassMark CPU and memory results. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 103.4 GB/sec. Tradeoffs include average multi-threaded stress performance and poor large-model LLM generation throughput due to lack of accelerators. The instance provides strong resource efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, large caching layers, compilation clusters, and mid-scale analytics pipelines.
